intent: Trace the percentage of African Americans living in the South over the years from 1790 to 2010 and compare the early twentieth-century level with the 1970 level.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
Trace the percentage of African Americans living in the South over the years from 1790 to 2010.
Compare the early twentieth-century level with the 1970 level.

units.claim: All 1 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: The African-American share living in the South remained near 90% from 1790 through 1910, then declined sharply to about 53% by 1970, reached a low of 52% in 1990, and rose slightly to 57% by 2010.
units.computation: Identify the overall trajectory from 1790 to 2010: stable high plateau (~90-93%) until 1910, steep decline 1910-1970 (90% to 53%), minimum 52% at 1990, slight increase to 57% at 2010.
accept: Describes a long high plateau near 90% from 1790 to 1910.
Notes a sharp decline between 1910 and 1970.
Mentions the low point around 1990 (52%) and slight rise to 2010 (57%).
reject: Claims a monotonic increase or no change over the period.
Omits the early stable period or the post-1970 slight rise.
Uses data points not in the table.

units.claim: The early twentieth-century level (1910: 90%) was substantially higher than the 1970 level (53%), a difference of 37 percentage points.
units.computation: Compare value at 1910 (90%) with value at 1970 (53%); absolute difference = 37 percentage points.
accept: States that the early twentieth-century level (1910) was about 90%.
States that the 1970 level was about 53%.
Notes the large drop of roughly 37 percentage points.
reject: Compares 1970 with a different early twentieth-century year without justification.
Gives incorrect values for either year.

optional_valid: Mentions that the maximum value (93%) occurred in 1810 and 1830.
Notes that the minimum value (52%) occurred in 1990.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for the decline (e.g., Great Migration) not present in the table.
Data points for years not listed in the table (e.g., 1800, 1900).
Comparisons with other demographic groups or regions not in the table.
review_notes: The intent asks to trace the percentage over 1790-2010 and compare early 20th-century level with 1970. Two semantic units cover these operations.
Early twentieth-century level is interpreted as 1910, the closest anchor year in the table before the decline.
